meta.notes: Revised source list with verified URLs. Sources without native RSS use polling, scraping, or GovWire fallbacks. validation.method: Web search verification of all feed URLs, page URLs, and content types
validation.summary: 11 RSS feeds verified, 11 scrape/API fallbacks verified, 2 newsletters verified. All source pages confirmed active.

sources.name: Artificial Lawyer
sources.notes: Primary legal AI source. Covers product launches, funding, firm adoption.

sources.name: Legal IT Insider
sources.notes: No public RSS. Scrape or use email-to-RSS bridge on their newsletter.

sources.name: Legal Futures
sources.notes: Legal business and innovation. Good on firm strategy and SRA policy.

sources.name: SRA News and Updates
sources.notes: SRA confirms RSS available via news page. Also has separate decisions RSS. Scrape fallback if feed URL changes.

sources.name: SRA Consultations
sources.notes: Separate from general SRA news. Catches AI/innovation consultations early.

sources.name: Law Society Gazette
sources.notes: Broad legal profession coverage. Filter for tech/AI/regulation keywords.

sources.name: Legal Cheek
sources.notes: Surprisingly good at breaking stories about firms adopting AI. High volume -- keyword filter essential.

sources.name: Free Movement
sources.notes: Core immigration law commentary. Relevant to Lawyery's practice area.

sources.name: ICO Blog and News
sources.notes: ICO RSS currently broken (site redesign). Poll the news page. Critical for AI + data protection overlap.

sources.name: UK Parliament Science, Innovation and Technology Committee
sources.notes: AI inquiries and evidence sessions. Low volume but high impact when relevant.

sources.name: Migration Advisory Committee
sources.notes: GovWire RSS verified. GOV.UK Content API as fallback. Essential for immigration practice.

sources.name: Home Office Immigration Rules and Policy
sources.notes: GovWire RSS verified. Catches statement of changes, policy guidance updates.

sources.name: OIMC (formerly OISC)
sources.notes: GovWire RSS verified. Regulatory updates for immigration advisers. Low volume.

sources.name: Anthropic Blog
sources.notes: No official RSS. Community-maintained feed on GitHub (taobojlen/anthropic-rss-feed). Scrape fallback if community feed goes stale.

sources.name: Harvey AI Blog
sources.notes: No RSS. Leading legal AI company -- product announcements and case studies.

sources.name: Luminance Blog
sources.notes: No RSS. UK-based legal AI. Contract review and due diligence focus.

sources.name: Clio Blog
sources.notes: Practice management + AI features. Good annual Legal Trends Report.

sources.name: Legal Evolution
sources.notes: Bill Henderson. Deep analysis on structural change in legal services. Low frequency, high quality.

sources.name: Ars Technica AI
sources.notes: Replaces TechCrunch and The Register. Better signal-to-noise for substantive AI coverage. Note: free RSS provides excerpts only.

sources.name: BAILII
sources.notes: Searchable RSS. Configure for immigration tribunal and AI-related judgments.

sources.name: Hacker News (filtered)
sources.notes: Using hnrss.org for keyword-filtered feed. More reliable than raw HN RSS.

sources.name: arXiv cs.AI
sources.notes: Replaced cs.CL with cs.AI -- catches more legal-relevant work. Keyword filter essential.

sources.name: Damien Charlotin AI Hallucination Database
sources.notes: Auto-discovered. Maintains comprehensive database of AI hallucination cases in legal proceedings with 1,316 cases identified. Frequently cited by courts and media as authoritative source.. Initial assessment: Very high - academic researcher at HEC Paris, database cited in judicial decisions and major media outlets.

sources.name: The Ethics Reporter
sources.notes: Auto-discovered. Provides in-depth analysis of AI sanctions and ethical issues in legal practice. Recent coverage of record-breaking sanctions suggests valuable ongoing coverage.. Initial assessment: Good - detailed reporting on legal ethics issues with specific case citations and data analysis.

sources.name: Solicitor News
sources.notes: Auto-discovered. UK-focused legal publication covering regulatory developments and technology adoption in English legal market, particularly strong on SRA and Ministry of Justice developments. Initial assessment: Professional legal publication with good sourcing and regular updates on regulatory developments.

sources.name: AI Funding Tracker
sources.notes: Auto-discovered. Comprehensive tracking of AI startup funding with detailed coverage of legal AI sector, including funding amounts, valuations and strategic context. Initial assessment: Specialized data source with detailed funding information, appears to have good industry connections.

newsletters.notes: These require an email-to-RSS bridge service (kill-the-newsletter.com, Feedbin, or similar). Subscribe with a bridge address, then poll the resulting feed.

sources.name: Legaltech Hub Newsletter
sources.notes: Product launches, funding rounds, market analysis. Surfaces things before RSS outlets.

sources.name: Law Society Technology and Law Policy Updates
sources.notes: Distinct from the Gazette. Covers AI guidance, ethical frameworks, practice notes.
